newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices seen rangebound, eyes on INRO.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices seen rangebound, eyes on INRO.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are expected to drift in a narrow range next week, as the focus will be on whether the International Natural Rubber Organization (INRO) will enter the market to support prices, Japanese traders said on Friday.
They added, however, they were rather sceptical that INRO's market intervention would have a significant effect on prices.
"Rubber prices may drift narrowly next week in an attempt to consolidate recent sharp falls," an analyst at a commodity broker said. "Focus is on the volume INRO buys, if it does intervene," he said.
Rising output and expected slow physical demand from consumers during the summer have cast a shadow on the market.
"Market sentiment here is basically bearish as supplies are excessive in rubber producing countries," the analyst said.
INRO's five-day indicator for rubber prices fell below 183 Malaysia/Singapore cents a kg on Friday, a level at which INRO may buy rubber in the market.
An INRO official said on Friday the group could enter the market "anytime" to support rubber prices if they stay at the current rate or slipped to the "must buy" level of 172 cents.
Benchmark December rubber futures on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 114.6 yen per kg on Friday, against Thursday's close of 112.0 yen.
Benchmark December rubber on the Kobe Rubber Exchange, was quoted at 114.5 yen, compared with 112.6 yen on Thursday.
Another commodity analyst said that even if prices recovered after INRO's possible intervention, private investors would probably jump on the opportunity to sell.

"Private investors are waiting for any price rebound to sell. The topside at 116.0 yen or 117.0 yen for TOCOM benchmark December would be hard to break through as selling can be expected," the analyst said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 90.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, against 95.00 U.S. cents on July 4.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 119.0 yen per kg as of Friday, against 122.0 yen a week ago.
